Android Auto Cielo Update Could Include More Surprises, Android Auto 18.1 Code Shows
9 photos
Photo: Google
The Cielo update is undoubtedly a highly anticipated Android Auto update, and the closer we get to its launch, the more surprises are being discovered. This time, the newly released Android Auto 18.1 includes evidence that Google might be aiming for something that would make perfect sense: sync the debut of Cielo with the introduction of a new light theme.
It’s already feeling like Google has been working on the Android Auto light mode for ages, with evidence of these visual tweaks being in development spotted long ago.
But now it turns out that the search giant is making good progress on this front, and the new light theme is being developed side by side with the Cielo makeover. The objective might be a synced debut, so the introduction of Cielo, which will bring widgets and other new features, could also include a light mode.
A recent teardown of the Android Auto 18.1 APK includes mentions of the light mode being developed for Samsung phones, though there’s a very good chance that these tweaks are also planned for other Android devices, such as Google Pixel phones. Google wants the redesign to be available in both dark and light modes, so there’s no doubt that the same assets would eventually be available for all devices running Android Auto.
Google also seems to be making progress in the development of Cielo, with Android Auto 18.1 including mentions of the animations we’ll see when we interact with the redesigned interface.
The company has so far remained tight-lipped as to when we’re supposed to get our hands on Cielo, but considering all these new releases include more and more evidence that the update is coming, it’s probably safe to assume that the “coming soon” promise is actually happening this time.
The first beta users could get the new interface by the end of the year, and I expect the rollout to production devices to begin in the first quarter of 2027 before gaining more traction during the summer.
Photo: Google The Cielo update Google wants to completely transform the Android Auto experience in a way that makes more sense in new-generation cars.
This is why Android Auto will use the available screen estate more efficiently, no matter the shape, dimensions, or resolution. Right now, Android Auto is often centered and displayed in a rectangular panel on infotainment screens with unusual designs, and the introduction of Cielo will change that. The best example is the circular screen installed in MINI cars, where Android Auto will use the entire screen estate to run its apps, including Google Maps.
Google also wants the experience with Android Auto to feel smoother and more fluid. And because the purpose of Android Auto is to be an extension of Android, it’ll get new fonts and smoother animations, such as the ones that are currently being worked on and spotted in Android Auto 18.1.
Photo: Google Wallpapers will get new features and will be allowed to roam between devices when the user experience transitions from a phone to a car. The same wallpaper could appear on both screens, making the switch from one screen to the other smoother.
Google is also planning to unlock new app categories, and without a doubt, the topic that’s getting the most attention this time is the introduction of video apps. Google will finally enable YouTube videos on Android Auto , and the company even promises 60 fps full HD support in cars where such capabilities are possible.
The YouTube support will enable drivers to watch videos when their cars are stationary, while an audio-only mode will allow them to continue playback by listening to the audio track. Video playback will be locked when the car is in motion as a safety restriction. YouTube will require a Premium subscription for such capabilities, considering the ability to play videos in the background is not part of the free tier.
Photo: Google The last big update that’ll go live as part of the Cielo makeover is the integration of widgets. The long-term objective is to allow all Android applications that can show widgets on mobile devices to expand to Android Auto, but it’s unclear if this functionality will be available at launch.
Once widgets go live, the Android Auto UI will be divided into more floating panels appearing on the screen at the same time. Google Maps will be in the background and expand to the edges of the screen, while the rest of the apps, such as the media card on the Coolwalk screen, will be displayed as a floating panel.
Widgets will be displayed on the right of the screen, and users will be able to see the weather, the clock, their calendar entries, and pretty much anything that a widget shows without opening the full apps.
Considering the Cielo update is still in the works, many of these specifics might change before the rollout begins. However, Google’s original teasers certainly looked promising, and fingers crossed that it won’t take long before we get our hands on the same goodies.
